tasks.task:
Close these in r17; no id/envelope changes; blocker if impossible. Round 6 of loop rounds 6-8.
1 F1 HIGH cross-family symlink target unprotected: R2/section 8 promise any symlinked target is never touched, but R5/section 4 protect only within the moved family's pass and assume a foreign target was never a candidate. Counterexamples: (A) snapshot.json is a relative symlink to pre-existing prompts.corrupt-<X> and both families are corrupt; the snapshot pass protects nothing (foreign target), then the prompts pass evicts X oldest-first, leaving snapshot.corrupt-<now>.json dangling and the rejected bytes deleted on the successful path. (B) prompts.json is a relative symlink to snapshot.corrupt-<X> older than the newest four; the snapshot pass runs first and unlinks X before the prompts family is examined, then prompts.json's Stat resolves ErrNotExist and recovery silently no-ops. Fix by specifying a run-level protected-target set that both family passes consult, populated from every moved link entry including the link of a family not yet examined when the other family runs first (resolve relative link targets with explicit rules for in-directory and out-of-directory targets, and state the behavior when the target is absent, is a directory, is not a conforming quarantine name, or is the configured path itself). Keep the same-family behavior already accepted in r16 (protected candidate excluded from eviction, oldest-first skips to the next-oldest unprotected, bound stays QuarantineKeep on success). Add a cross-family subcase under existing AC1-3 and AC1-10 with both counterexamples, target-byte-preserved, quarantine-read-through (where a quarantine exists), explicit survivor counts, and a same-pass ordering assertion for case B. Do not weaken preservation to satisfy retention tests.
2 F2 MEDIUM section 4 step (3) candidate set contradicts R5/AC1-3: candidates are defined as pre-existing files beyond the four newest slots, then minus the protected file; with AC1-3's own five seeds and the protected oldest this leaves an empty set and six retained, contradicting R5 ('protected file occupies one of the four slots'), AC1-3 (now-4s unlinked, total 5) and section 8. Define candidates as all unprotected pre-existing conforming files of that family, oldest-first, attempted until exactly four pre-existing files survive; keep the protected file excluded from the candidate list and state that it holds one of the four surviving pre-existing slots. Align section 4, R5, D10 and section 8 wording.
3 F3 LOW: wiring.go:486-494 is cited as the off-arm block, but :494 is the next case; the block is 486-493 with :486 and the remediation at :492. Correct every occurrence.
4 F4 LOW: section 9.7 omits ticket line 11's second stale reference SNAPREC-SPEC-r3. Record it (heading r15, header r7, second stale reference r3), keeping the ticket-mirror lag account.
5 F5 LOW: AC1-3's symlink subcase and AC1-10(b-prot) never state the seeded target must be a store-rejected corrupt file; 'exactly one Recovery' only implies it. State the seeded target is rejected/raises ErrCorrupt under Load so the link entry itself is what recovery classifies and moves.
Return the full nine-section spec, unchanged ids, and a change log mapping each finding to its closing text.
